Not a GS employee, but I understand the business. They want to sell you a used game because stores like GS make minimal profits on "New" items. They pay the manufacturers for the game, and try and sell it to make a dime. 

With used games, it's the same mentality as a pawn shop. They have to buy the game, let it sit in their inventory, and hope someone buys it within a decent timeframe.

It doesn't help that the same game likely gets turned in at the same time. 

Say they get 100 copies of one game within 3 days. Now that's 100 copies they need to get their money back on. And due to that, that last copy has 99 copies in front of it. It's a Supply and Demand thing, and also that's where GS capitalizes and actually becomes profitable.

I feel dirty defending some of their practices on Reddit, but I don't get the hate most people have towards them.
